name: rizin
desc: UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset
why: A full UNIX-style reverse engineering framework that opens binaries, firmware, and running programs to inspection.

brief.what_it_is: Rizin is a free, open-source reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. You point it at a binary, firmware image, or running program, and it gives you disassembly, analysis, and inspection through an interactive shell (the `rizin` command) or through separate single-purpose tools such as rz-bin, rz-asm, and rz-hash. The README describes it as usable for analyzing binaries, disassembling code, debugging programs, forensics, and as a scriptable command-line hex editor that can open disk files. The Cutter GUI sits on top of the same backend.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says Rizin takes a unique, Unix-friendly approach to reverse engineering, aiming for a shell-like environment for analyzing binaries from the command line "without unnecessary weight", while still providing a base for GUIs and scripting. The GitHub README says it was "born as a fork of the radare2, with a focus on usability, features and cleanliness."
brief.how_it_works: The `rizin` shell is built on a backend that analyzes binary formats and architectures; the homepage says the shell was redesigned using Tree-sitter for grammar parsing, with commands registered in YAML files to drive help text. A new analysis step matches unnamed functions in stripped binaries against FLIRT signatures from sigdb. Scripting goes through rzpipe, which the README says supports Python, Haskell, OCaml, Ruby, Rust, and Go.

commands_seen.context: Clone the source repository before building from source.
Configure the build directory from source using meson.
Compile Rizin in the build directory.
Install the built Rizin system-wide (needs sudo).
Start the interactive shell; it prints a banner and drops to a prompt like [0x00000000]>.
Suggested way to get meson at least version 0.55.0 if the system package is older.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew: the formula's caveats say plugins, extras and bindings are installed at $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/rizin. Building from source needs meson 0.55.0 or newer (pip install meson is suggested), and a meson setup / compile / sudo install sequence; the README points to BUILDING.md for more detail. The README links to rizin.re/install for other install methods. No accounts or API keys are mentioned. Scripting from other languages needs the separate rzpipe library.
brief.standout: The shell is rebuilt on Tree-sitter with commands defined in YAML, and the analysis step applies FLIRT signatures to unnamed functions so common library code in stripped binaries is labelled automatically. It also has a beta project format for saving and loading whole sessions, and a package manager (rz-pm) for plugins.
brief.status: Unknown from the sources read. The README and homepage show no release date, last-commit date, or version number. The homepage calls it "a new project" and describes the projects feature as beta and rz-pm as early development, so it is active but young. I did not check the repository's commit history.
brief.caveats: Several features are still early: the project save/load format is beta and rz-pm is in early development. Building from source needs a recent meson and a sudo install step. The README lists broad support (Windows 7+, macOS, Linux, BSDs, Android, QNX, Solaris, Haiku, and many CPU architectures), but the list is long and I did not verify depth of support per architecture. The brew caveat notes plugin paths live under the Homebrew prefix.
